subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: What default security policy should OpenClaw apply before externally or plugin-registered recurring agentTurn cron jobs can run on an inherited model?
rationale: The source reproduction is clear, but the fix changes cron activation defaults, plugin scheduling contracts, provider/model cost policy, persisted state, and upgrade/doctor behavior, so automation cannot safely choose the boundary.

options.title: Coordinated Cron Safety Policy
options.body: Require operator-visible activation or approval for recurring external/plugin agentTurn jobs, add model-cost visibility, and pair any breaking default with doctor/update migration guidance.

options.title: Narrow Model-Cost Guard
options.body: Keep current activation semantics but warn or block when a recurring agentTurn job inherits an expensive default model without an explicit job model.

options.title: Split into narrow tracked work
options.body: Keep this issue as the consent/provenance canonical item and route circuit breakers and budgets to the existing related issues.

recommendation.title: Coordinated Cron Safety Policy
recommendation.body: Require operator-visible activation or approval for recurring external/plugin agentTurn jobs, add model-cost visibility, and pair any breaking default with doctor/update migration guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history signal is on both cron service behavior and the plugin scheduled-turn bridge that reproduces the issue.
